summary: Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930–2014) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1949–1953). He served as a lecturer at Bigakko, Kokugakuin, and Tama Art universities, and professor at Joshibi University (~1989–1996).

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his D.Lit. at Bukkyo University by 1993, later serving there as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1952) and completed a doctorate at Toyo University by 1962, where he served as assistant professor (~1964–1992).
Shuyu Sakurai (b. 1916) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University from ~1940 to 1943 and held a post at Komazawa University from ~1958 to 1987, becoming professor emeritus.

Shwe Zan Aung (1871–1932) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a B.A. at the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.
Shōkō Kabutogi (1912–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University from ~1933 to 1936 and later served there as a professor from ~1962 to 1983.

Shōren Ihara (1923–1999) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1977) and the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998), teaching Hiromasa Tosaki and Kunio Harikai.

Shōyū Hanayama (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1957), served as vice president of Musashino University (~1970–1995), and chaired Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (~1990–1995).

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014). He also studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and Sayadaw U Ghosita.

Sibani Das Gupta is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She earned a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibaraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah, and served as lecturer of philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

Sibnath Sarma is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir and as philosophy professor at Gauhati University (attested 1999–2012), teaching Sibaraj Chetry, Namita Das, and Loukram Ibempishak Devi.
Sibylle Koch specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Oxford and earned an MA from the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2012–2015).

Sicheng Liang (1901–1972) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Beijing Huiwen Middle School, Tsinghua University (~1915–1923), and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (~1924–1927), and held a post at Peking University.

Sidney Lee (1859–1926) was an academic who studied at the City of London School (~1872–1878) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882). He held a post at Queen Mary University of London from ~1913 to 1924.

Siegbert Hummel (1908–2001) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied across Tübingen, Rostock, Munich, and Leipzig (PhD 1932–1938), later studying under Eduard Erkes and others (~1946–1948). He curated the Asian Department at Leipzig's Museum of Ethnography (1947–1955).

Siegfried Behrsing (1903–1994) worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Greifswald, Tübingen, and Leipzig (Ph.D. 1924–1930) under scholars including Friedrich Weller. He held posts at Leipzig, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Humboldt University (1953–1969).

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867), Göttingen, and Paris under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, and Theodor Benfey. He was a professor at the University of Strasbourg (1871, 1881).

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) was an Indologist who studied at Vienna (Dr. phil. 1946–1949), Paris, and Stockholm (Habilitation ~1958–1960). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Kiel University, Stockholm University (professor 1968–1990), and the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

Siglinde Dietz (b. 1944) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied under Frank-Richard Hamm and earned a PhD under Michael Hahn at the University of Bonn (-1980). She held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
